newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Chamber approves end-of-year finance package.
newsitem.headline: Italy Chamber approves end-of-year finance package.

text.p: Italy's Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Thursday approved the final piece of its 1997 budget after an marathon sitting.
The vote was approved by 207 votes to 167 with one abstention. The measure now becomes law since no changes were made to the text already approved by the Senate (upper house).
Italy's centre-left government resorted to a confidence vote on Tuesday to sweep aside filibustering amendments presented by the opposition to the package of measures.
It won that vote with ease but parliamentary rules require a further vote on the item of legislation itself.

The debate was held up again on Wednesday night after 143 opposition deputies, mostly from the far-right National Alliance party, said they would exercise a right to speak for up to 10 minutes each before the vote.
The Democratic Party of the Left, the biggest in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government, condemned the tactic as "infantile" and called for proceedings to go on through the night.

Italy has adopted a series of increasingly tough budgets over the past five years in a bid to repair the damage done by free-spending administrations at the end of the 1980s and become a founder member of the single European currency.
The latest budget, which was mostly approved by parliament last December, was designed to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($37.2 billion) off the public sector deficit in 1997.
However the final segment, which accounts for 4.3 trillion lire of savings, was only introduced as a cabinet decree. ($1=1,678)
